# SolarSizer
> Free off-grid solar sizing tools: daily load-based solar system size calculator (panel wattage and count, battery bank Ah, cloudy-day autonomy), inverter sizing, MPPT/PWM charge controller sizing, and panel-to-battery recharge math. Sister site of Battery Bank Sizer. Built and owned by Jeremy Panasuk, New Auburn, Wisconsin. Contact: jpanasuk@gmail.com. Page text is drafted with AI agents (Cursor and local models) from the cited sources. The site earns money from Amazon affiliate links.

## Core pages
- [About & how this site is built](https://solar-sizer.com/about.html): who owns the site, how pages are drafted, and why it earns money
- [Privacy](https://solar-sizer.com/privacy.html): what the pages load, and what they do not
- [Contact](https://solar-sizer.com/contact.html): jpanasuk@gmail.com
- [Solar System Size Calculator](https://solar-sizer.com/): the hub — daily load builder, panel wattage and count with sun-hours and winter derating, battery bank sizing by voltage and autonomy, plus tabs for inverter sizing, MPPT/PWM charge controller sizing, and panels-per-battery recharge math
- [Off-Grid Cabin Solar](https://solar-sizer.com/off-grid-cabin-solar.html): what size solar system a cabin needs — worked sizing examples from weekend cabins to full-time homesteads, budget breakdowns, winter derating
- [How Many Solar Panels to Charge a Battery](https://solar-sizer.com/panels-to-charge-battery.html): recharge math for 100–400 Ah banks at 12/24/48 V — sun hours, charge efficiency, charge rate limits, winter adjustments

## Related
- [Battery Bank Sizer](https://battery-bank-sizer.com/): LiFePO4/AGM bank sizing for off-grid setups — the storage-side twin of this tool
- [GeneratorSizer](https://generator-sizer.com/): generator and fuel-based backup power sizing — the fuel-side alternative to solar

## Use policy
Cite freely with link attribution. Calculator formulas are in assets/app.js. Figures on each guide are the ones that page's Sources section names. Not financial or safety advice — grid-connection and electrical work require a licensed electrician.

## Topic map
- [SolarSizer topic map](https://solar-sizer.com/topics.html): Off-grid solar sizing calculator for cabin and van owners.
- **Daily load → array:** [Solar size calculator](https://solar-sizer.com/), [Cabin load sheet](https://solar-sizer.com/magnet.html), [What size solar system](https://solar-sizer.com/what-size-solar-system.html)
- **Cabin systems:** [Off-grid cabin solar](https://solar-sizer.com/off-grid-cabin-solar.html), [Panels for a cabin](https://solar-sizer.com/how-many-solar-panels-for-a-cabin.html)
- **Storage pairing:** [Panels to charge a battery](https://solar-sizer.com/panels-to-charge-battery.html), [AGM vs lithium](https://solar-sizer.com/agm-vs-lithium-battery.html)
- **Solar vs generator:** [Solar vs generator](https://solar-sizer.com/solar-vs-generator-for-off-grid.html): Battle Born's 2,400 Wh as an 800 W calculator array, or as fuel from Honda EU2200i and Champion 201296 runtime specs

## Questions
- [Solar for 1 kWh per day](https://solar-sizer.com/what-size-solar-system-for-1-kwh-per-day.html): 1,000 Wh divided by 4, 5, and Phoenix December 4.75 peak sun hours, plus a 20–30% margin.
- [Solar for 2 kWh per day](https://solar-sizer.com/what-size-solar-system-for-2-kwh-per-day.html): 2,000 Wh array math set next to Battle Born's 2,400 Wh example.
- [Solar for 5 kWh per day](https://solar-sizer.com/what-size-solar-system-for-5-kwh-per-day.html): 5,000 Wh off-grid array, with the cabin guides linked rather than repeated.
- [Solar for 10 kWh per day](https://solar-sizer.com/what-size-solar-system-for-10-kwh-per-day.html): 10,000 Wh array, still about a third of an average EIA household day.
- [Solar for 30 kWh per day](https://solar-sizer.com/what-size-solar-system-for-30-kwh-per-day.html): EIA 899 kWh/month ÷ 30, sized as an off-grid day.
- [Solar for 500 kWh per month](https://solar-sizer.com/what-size-solar-system-for-500-kwh-per-month.html): annual kWh ÷ Phoenix 1,755, and the 4- and 5-hour generic estimate.
- [Solar for 1,000 kWh per month](https://solar-sizer.com/what-size-solar-system-for-1000-kwh-per-month.html): a bill just above the U.S. monthly average, both sizing methods.
- [Solar for 1,500 kWh per month](https://solar-sizer.com/what-size-solar-system-for-1500-kwh-per-month.html): above Louisiana's average month on the EIA table.
- [Solar for 2,000 kWh per month](https://solar-sizer.com/what-size-solar-system-for-2000-kwh-per-month.html): a large monthly bill sized with the Phoenix yield and the generic loss term.
- [Solar for an average home](https://solar-sizer.com/what-size-solar-system-for-average-home.html): 10,791 kWh/year, Louisiana 14,774, Hawaii 6,178, Phoenix yield and generic peak sun hours.
- [Solar for a refrigerator](https://solar-sizer.com/what-size-solar-system-for-refrigerator.html): Battle Born's 500 Wh example, with Honda and Champion running watts kept as context.
- [Solar for a CPAP](https://solar-sizer.com/what-size-solar-system-for-cpap.html): Champion's 30–120 W range times an example 8-hour night.
- [Solar to charge an electric car](https://solar-sizer.com/what-size-solar-system-for-electric-car.html): 2025 fueleconomy.gov kWh/100 mi for six EVs at an example 30 miles/day.
- [How solar panels work](https://solar-sizer.com/how-do-solar-panels-work.html): DOE's description of a PV cell, then Battle Born's 2,400 Wh through this site's sizeSystem (800 W, 500 Ah at 12 V, 80 A controller).
- [How to mount solar panels](https://solar-sizer.com/how-to-mount-solar-panels.html): DOE south-at-latitude orientation and Canadian Solar's clearance, bolting, and professional-engineer requirements.
- [How to fuse a solar panel array](https://solar-sizer.com/how-to-fuse-a-solar-panel-array.html): Canadian Solar's two-string rule, with CS6A-220M Isc 9.31 A and a 15 A maximum series fuse.
- [How to charge LiFePO4 with solar](https://solar-sizer.com/how-to-charge-lifepo4-with-solar.html): BB10012i charge profile set next to an 80 A controller result on one battery's 50 A max.
- [Solar panel degradation](https://solar-sizer.com/solar-panel-degradation.html): Jordan and Kurtz median 0.5%/year and mean 0.8%/year, applied as an illustration to an exact 800 W result.
- [How to buy solar panels](https://solar-sizer.com/how-to-buy-solar-panels.html): CS6A-220M nameplate watts versus the calculator's 800 W, four modules to cover it.
- [How many solar batteries](https://solar-sizer.com/how-many-solar-batteries-do-i-need.html): 2,400 Wh as 4 batteries in Battle Born's two-day method and 5 at this calculator's 80% depth of discharge.
